trust_decision.summary: Which secret values (HTTP header values, TOML config values, session tokens, SSE-C keys, signed-URL params) may reach the driver log; decided per log call site, with a regex mask in internal/logger applied to every formatted message as the only central backstop.

landing_point.why: Advisory says the driver writes sensitive info to logs; the first grep hit for header dumps is the 'Header: %v' line in the main query REST helper postRestfulQueryHelper.

fix_sites.entry_point: connect with Okta authenticator -> postAuthOKTA failure path
connect with Okta authenticator -> getSSO failure path
large result set fetch -> downloadChunkHelper with server chunkHeaders (SSE-C key)
every logger call via secretMaskingLogger -> MaskSecrets (also exported via secret_detector.go:7)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: internal/logger/secret_detector.go:14 (connectionTokenPattern value class lacks ':' so 'ver:1-hint:...' session tokens are never masked) and internal/config/connection_configuration.go:278 (TOML loader WARN logs every key's value, incl. password, on the success path)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about HTTP header dumps; the TOML loader is a separate config package (and the success-path WARN looks like a harmless diagnostic), and the masking regex is 'already there', so a solver can argue both belong to other features.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Header NAMES and TOML key names must still be logged for diagnostics (fix tests assert 'Parsed key: password' is still present), status/URL lines stay; masking must not swallow non-secret neighbours (sasTokenPattern replacement changed to '${1}=****'). Removing all logging, or masking every value-looking token, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: http.Header rendered with %v as map[Name:[value]] (not matched by header patterns)
map[string]string chunk header key/value pair (SSE-C customer key)
TOML value of any type (string/int/bool) passed as any
signed-URL query params X-Amz-Credential / X-Amz-Security-Token with %-escapes

O7_producer.where: fmt %v rendering of http.Header at restful.go:332 (and chunk_downloader.go:440, heartbeat.go:103) produces map[Name:[value]]; masking at internal/logger/secret_detector.go:41-47 only sees the rendered string

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Chunk download non-200 path logs resp.Header with %v inside a combined line; published fix changed only the chunk-header request line above it
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Debug-level, and header dumped inline with status/URL/body rather than as a standalone 'Header: %v' line, so a grep for the report's pattern misses it; changelog lists only restful/auth/authokta/heartbeat as header-dump sites
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same root package, different file from landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Heartbeat success path logs the whole *http.Response with %v, which includes the Header map
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Success (200) path at Debug level and it formats resp, not resp.Header, so it does not look like a header dump; fix only touched the failure line 125 in the same function
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as a fix site (heartbeat.go:125)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: TOML parse error returns SnowflakeError whose MessageArgs carry the raw value, so the secret survives into the error text callers log
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a returned error, not a driver log line; the driver itself does not log it (driver.go:28-29)
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: internal/config package, two packages from landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Arrow-stream batch path copies Qrmk/ChunkHeaders into its own downloader; a debug log of the headers it attaches there
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Second chunk-fetch implementation for arrowbatches; maintainers mirror the chunk_downloader.go:414-418 debug loop when porting.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: storage clients (S3/Azure/GCS) logging presigned URLs or response headers on failure
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already logs a presigned URL at debug; a header dump on a failed PUT/GET mirrors restful.go failure-path style and lives in a different transport (file transfer).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: OAuth token-request failure path logging resp.Header / token response body
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same failure-path idiom as auth.go:229-230; OAuth responses carry access/refresh tokens in shapes the regex does not cover.

O9_family: CWE-532 sensitive information written to log files (log-sink redaction, multi-site plus central regex mask)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0 per go.mod:3 (repo CI supports up to Go 1.27)
O10_build.project_tests: internal/logger/secret_detector_test.go (MaskSecrets unit tests), internal/config/connection_configuration_test.go, util_test.go; root-package auth/restful tests use mocked FuncPost/FuncGet and wiremock (wiremock-based tests need a local wiremock process)

j.j_sites_touched: restful.go, auth.go, authokta.go, heartbeat.go, chunk_downloader.go, util.go, internal/config/connection_configuration.go, internal/logger/secret_detector.go
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a header-value regex to MaskSecrets (or mask the four restful.go 'Header: %v' lines) and stop, leaving the chunk_downloader/heartbeat %v dumps, the TOML success-path WARN and the colon-token regex gap open.
